source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:26 (the Masorah's four dageshed alefs)
claim_en: va-yaviu ('and they BROUGHT him the gift'): the alef carries a DAGESH — one of the Masorah's FOUR dageshed alefs in Scripture (the partner it names: 'and they brought to us, by the good hand of our God', Ezra 8:18; the file's other stations named at Lev and Job) — and SNAPSHOT writes the dot inside the guttural in-stream: the rarest mark in the corpus so far, pressed where the gift crosses Joseph's threshold.

va-yiqdu VA-YISHTACHU ('and they bowed their heads and prostrated'): the span's ketiv/qere lands on the BOW-WORD — written clipped (no final vav), read whole; SNAPSHOT carries the pair as two tokens, the bare written form beside the pointed read form, so the verse's word-count wears the doubling: nine tokens where the eye reads eight.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:2 (the Ramah; the Masorah)
claim_en: SHUVU shivru ('RETURN, buy'): lean at the father's bare demand (43:2; its twin at 44:25 also lean per the Ramah) — and the SAME chapter writes the verb FULL at the release: qumu SHUVU (43:13). The full skeleton stands exactly THREE times in the Torah — the release (43:13), the noun 'his return' (14:17, the collision framed), and the tents-return (Deut 5:30); the Ramah's third full imperative is the prefixed gate-run (Exod 32:27, named): lean toward Egypt empty-handed, full with the brother in hand.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:10; Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:10
claim_en: ki LULE hitmahmahnu ('for had we not lingered'): the had-not word ends in ALEF here, its ONLY such token in the Torah — everywhere else the word takes a final yod (Laban's field 31:42; the enemy's boast Deut 32:27, both asserted). And the Kitzur reads the same verse's seam: the last letters of ki ata SHAVNU ze ('for by now we could have returned') spell the four-letter Name in order (builder-asserted): the Name goes down with the caravan.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:4 (the Masorah)
claim_en: NERDA ('we will go down' / 'let us go down'): exactly TWICE in the Torah — Babel's divine plural ('let us go down and confuse', Gen 11:7) and the brothers' condition (43:4); the Masorah's third is Saul's night-pursuit (1 Sam 14:36, named): a descent that scatters tongues, and a descent that buys bread for one house.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:7 (the Ramah; the Hilleli; the Samuel pair)
claim_en: SHAOL shaal ('the man ASKED and asked'): the infinitive FULL with its vav (the Hilleli and every precise book; the Samuel pair named) — and the full skeleton's Torah census is a triple collision: the asking (43:7), the Edomite king Shaul (36:37-38, two tokens), and SHEOL the grave (Deut 32:22): to ask, a king, and the pit share one spelling — four tokens.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:7 (the Hilleli; Minchat Kohen)
claim_en: ha-YADOA neda ('could we KNOW, knowing'): its one Torah token, written FULL with the Hilleli copy, many precise books, and Minchat Kohen's none-other-and-full ruling — against Masorah-notes that divide and an old scroll-tikkun's variant: the stream keeps the vav.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:18 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi; Rashi; the Masorah)
claim_en: va-YIRU ha-anashim ('and the men FEARED'): written with BOTH yods — the Hilleli copy alone clips one; the Yerushalmi, every book, Rashi's own note ('written with two yods, and its Targum is fear'), and the Masorah's all-Torah-full rule stands verified across the stream: all SEVEN Torah tokens of the form carry both yods — Gerar's men (20:8), the bundles (42:35), the house (43:18), the sea twice (Exod 14:10, 14:31), the shining face (Exod 34:30), and Seir (Deut 2:4).

ha-kesef HA-SHAV ('the silver that was returned'): the CLIPPED participle — copies that write ha-MUSHAV here err by harmonizing the sons' word to the father's (43:12 ha-mushav, in-stream one chapter apart, asserted): the letter keeps the two returned-words distinct across six verses.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:15/29/31/33 (the Masorah)
claim_en: The feast's once-words, each its only Torah token: u-MISHNE kesef ('and double silver', 43:15); Elohim YACHNEKHA beni ('God be GRACIOUS to you, my son', 43:29 — checked; the priestly ויחנך ('and be gracious to you'), Num 6:25, wears the verb with a prefix-vav: collision framed — Joseph blesses the mother's son with the priests' verb before the priests exist); va-YITAPAQ ('and he RESTRAINED himself', 43:31 — the pair the Kitzur names: Haman restraining himself, Esther 5:10: both begin in sorrow and end in joy, each for its own house); ve-ha-TZAIR ('and the YOUNGEST', 43:33 — Isaiah's mighty-younger named). Three asserted, one checked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:34 (the Hilleli; the old print; the Masorah's portion-file)
claim_en: MI-MASOT kulam ('than the portions of them ALL'): written LEAN with the Hilleli, the earliest print, and every precise manuscript — an erring printer filled it against the Masorah's own four-token portion-file (this verse's two stations lean, its two others full; the vain-burdens pair, Lam 2:14, named by the Kitzur): Benjamin's five hands ride a lean word.

source: Minchat Shai + Chizkuni on Gen 43:8/10/11/15/20/29 (the chapter's file)
claim_en: The chapter's pointing file: ha-ZOT ('this', 43:15) with the zayin DAGESHED (checked); gam ('also', 43:8) gimel dageshed, peamim ('times', 43:10) pe soft, botnim ('pistachios', 43:11) bet in clipped qamatz (Chizkuni), lishbor ('to buy', 43:20) bet in clipped qamatz (Chizkuni), yachnekha (43:29) yod in clipped qamatz with resting chet (Chizkuni) — all asserted; named: shaal accented forward against the custom (43:7 — MS's lengthening-stroke excursus), the crowding-dagesh debate at u-mishne kesef (43:15).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:18 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi; the printed Masorah corrected)
claim_en: be-AMTACHTENU ('in our BAGS'): the Hilleli clips the yod, the Yerushalmi keeps it — and every one of our books keeps it (the printed Masorah's lean-note is the error MS corrects); the vav lean throughout the bag-word's family: the yod checked in-stream.
